vo: You can't put five products on one cert.
A certificate can describe only one product.
Five products means five certificates, one for each product.
Say the file shares one certificate across five different toys. That's the gap.

caption:
Five products on one certificate? That's one of the quietest gaps in a CPSC file.
Under 16 CFR 1110.13(a), each finished product certificate must describe only one product.
Five products usually means five certificates, each with its own product identifier, like a SKU or UPC.
Check that each CPSC certificate, a children's product certificate or a GCC, names one product and its own identifier.

sources.claim: Each certificate describes only one product
sources.quote: A finished product certificate must accompany each finished product or finished product shipment required to be certified pursuant to § 1110.5. Each finished product certificate must describe only one product.

sources.claim: Each certificate carries a product identifier
sources.quote: Finished product certificates must contain at least one of the following unique identifiers: global trade item number (GTIN), model number, registered number, serial number, stock keeping number (SKU), universal product code (UPC), or alternate identifier
